report_name: Malicious Calendar Invite Phishing Surges Over 30,000%

threat_actors.name: ICS Phishing Attackers
threat_actors.description: Unspecified threat actors leveraging malicious .ics calendar files to deliver Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools, a technique dubbed 'ICS phishing'.
threat_actors.goals: To gain persistent remote access to victim devices for data theft, credential harvesting, and potential ransomware deployment.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: Attackers send .ics calendar invites containing malicious links that, when clicked, direct victims to download and install malicious RMM tools like ScreenConnect.

attack_patterns.name: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: The attack relies on victims interacting with a malicious .ics calendar file sent via email. The file contains a lure and a link to download malware.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: Attackers trick victims into installing legitimate RMM tools like ScreenConnect to gain persistent remote access and full control over the compromised device.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware is a potential secondary payload deployed by attackers after gaining initial access, used to encrypt victim data for extortion.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: The overall attack is a form of phishing that uses .ics calendar invites sent from legitimate email services to bypass security filters and trick users.

tools.name: ScreenConnect
tools.description: A legitimate Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tool that attackers trick victims into installing to gain full control of the endpoint for data theft or secondary payload deployment.

infrastructure.name: Malware Hosting Sites
infrastructure.description: Websites used to host malicious RMM tool installers, which are linked from within the .ics calendar invites.

indicators.name: ScreenConnect Client Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: ScreenConnect Client Execution
id: 7e5f8a1b-9c0d-4e2f-8a1b-9c0d4e2f8a1b
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of ScreenConnect client, which can be abused by attackers for remote access.
references:
  - https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/keep-seeing-strange-meetings-and-events-in-your-calendar-it-might-be-because-calendar-based-phishing-has-jumped-33-000-percent-since-may-and-they-work-even-if-the-email-is-sent-to-spam
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-18
tags:
  - attack.t1219
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\ScreenConnect.Client.exe'
    OriginalFileName: 'ScreenConnect.Client.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of ScreenConnect for remote support.
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the ScreenConnect RMM tool, which is delivered via ICS phishing attacks.

indicators.name: Suspicious ICS Attachment from External Freemail
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious ICS Attachment from External Freemail Provider
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: Detects incoming emails with .ics calendar attachments from common external freemail providers, which is a TTP for ICS phishing.
references:
  - https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/keep-seeing-strange-meetings-and-events-in-your-calendar-it-might-be-because-calendar-based-phishing-has-jumped-33-000-percent-since-may-and-they-work-even-if-the-email-is-sent-to-spam
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-18
tags:
  - attack.t1566
  - attack.t1204.002
level: low
logsource:
  category: email
detection:
  selection_attachment:
    file_name|endswith: '.ics'
  selection_sender:
    sender|endswith:
      - '@gmail.com'
      - '@yahoo.com'
      - '@outlook.com'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate calendar invitations from external contacts using freemail services.
indicators.description: Detects incoming emails with .ics attachments from external, non-business email domains, a key indicator of ICS phishing.

relationships.source_name: Suspicious ICS Attachment from External Freemail
